drug_class: Combination Chemotherapy (Anthracycline + Antimetabolite) in a Liposomal Formulation
purpose: This medication is used to treat certain types of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), a cancer of the blood and bone marrow. It is specifically used for AML that has developed from a prior blood disorder or is related to previous cancer treatment. It combines two chemotherapy drugs in one injection to fight the cancer more effectively.
how_it_works: This medicine packages two chemotherapy drugs — daunorubicin and cytarabine — together inside tiny fat-like bubbles called liposomes. These bubbles help deliver both drugs directly to the cancer cells at the same time, in a specific ratio that has been shown to work best. Once inside the cancer cells, the drugs work together to block the cancer cells from growing and dividing, eventually destroying them.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, decreased appetite, mouth sores, fatigue, fever, swelling in arms or legs, rash, low blood cell counts (which can increase risk of infection, bleeding, or anemia), and headache.
warnings: This drug seriously lowers your blood counts, increasing your risk of life-threatening infections and bleeding — report any fever, chills, or unusual bleeding right away. It can also damage the heart, so your heart will be monitored before and during treatment. It should never be used in place of regular (non-liposomal) daunorubicin or cytarabine, as the dosing is very different and switching could be dangerous. It can harm an unborn baby, so effective birth control is important during treatment.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an IV infusion (into a vein) in a hospital or clinic over 90 minutes. It is typically given on Days 1, 3, and 5 of the first treatment cycle, and on Days 1 and 3 of any additional cycles if needed. Your doctor will determine the exact dose based on your body surface area (height and weight).
